define host-specific entomological parameters

Source: R/model_params.R
def_host_params.Rd

def_host_params This function can be used to load host-specific entomological parameters available in the package or to set the entomological parameters to new custom values provided by the user. Host parameters (biting, survival, and infection probabilities for humans and animals) are species-independent: the same values apply regardless of mosquito species.

Usage

def_host_params(host_table = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

host_table

data frame with custom host-specific values. Must be provided if custom parameter values should be used instead of the ones in the package database. The provided data frame should have the same structure (column names) as the database object host_ent_param. Default value is NULL.

verbose

boolean specifying whether any messages should be displayed during the execution of the function. Default value is TRUE.

Value

list object with the following vector attributes:

  • species_name: name of the mosquito species of the table row (if present; the values do not depend on it)

  • host: c("human", "animal")

  • PBi: probability that a mosquito that has encountered host i bites it (and survives to do so); mosquitoes failing a stage die

  • PCi: probability that a mosquito finds a resting place after biting a host of type i

  • PDi: probability that a mosquito survives the resting phase after biting a host of type i

  • PEi: probability that a mosquito lays eggs and returns to host seeking after resting, having bitten a host of type i

  • Kvi: proportion of susceptible mosquitoes that become infected after biting any host of type i

Each vector has two elements: (1) humans (without intervention) and (2) animals, in this order whatever the row order of host_table. Protected humans are added by the intervention functions.

Examples

# Retrieve the host-specific entomological parameters
hosts_p = def_host_params()

# Print all the parameters
print(hosts_p)
#> $species_name
#> [1] "Anopheles gambiae" "Anopheles gambiae"
#> 
#> $host
#> [1] "human"  "animal"
#> 
#> $PBi
#> [1] 0.95 0.95
#> 
#> $PCi
#> [1] 0.95 0.95
#> 
#> $PDi
#> [1] 0.99 0.99
#> 
#> $PEi
#> [1] 0.88 0.88
#> 
#> $Kvi
#> [1] 0.03 0.00
#>
